title.en: Inside ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2: How a Cross-Encoder Scores Relevance

description.en: Bi-encoders never actually read your query and document together â€” cross-encoders do. Meet ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2, the reranker that powers stage two of modern retrieval, build a toy pair-scorer, and wire up the full recall-then-rerank pipeline.

story_variants.en:
## The Model That Reads Both Sides

"Here's a secret about vector search," Vaathiyaar begins. "The embedding model never actually *reads your query and the document together*. all-MiniLM-L6-v2 compresses each text into 384 numbers **separately**, before it knows what question you'll ask. Cosine similarity then compares two summaries written in isolation. That's why the best answer sometimes ranks 7th â€” the summary threw away the one detail your query cared about. **cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2** fixes exactly this: it takes the query and one candidate document as a *single input*, lets attention flow between every query token and every document token, and outputs one number â€” a relevance score."

### Two Siblings, Two Contracts

Both models share the same 6-layer MiniLM backbone, but they end differently: the bi-encoder ends in mean pooling (a vector out), the cross-encoder ends in a classification head (a score out). That tiny change flips the economics completely:

| | Bi-encoder (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) | Cross-encoder (ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2) |
|---|---|---|
| Reads | one text at a time | query + document **together** |
| Outputs | 384-dim vector | single relevance score |
| Precompute? | yes â€” embed millions of docs once | no â€” score depends on the query |
| Cost per query | one embed + fast index lookup | one forward pass **per pair** |
| Best role | Stage 1: cast a wide net (recall) | Stage 2: pick the winners (precision) |

It was trained on **MS MARCO** â€” a million real Bing queries with human-marked relevant passages â€” so it has seen more "does this passage answer this question?" examples than any human librarian ever will.

### The Two-Stage Pipeline

Because the cross-encoder can't precompute anything, you never run it over the whole corpus. You let cheap vector search nominate ~50 candidates, then rerank only those:

```python
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

model = CrossEncoder("cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2")

query = "how do I speed up pandas joins?"
candidates = vector_search(query, top_k=50)   # stage 1: bi-encoder recall

pairs = [(query, doc) for doc in candidates]
scores = model.predict(pairs)                  # stage 2: joint scoring

reranked = [d for d, s in sorted(zip(candidates, scores),
                                 key=lambda p: p[1], reverse=True)]
top_5 = reranked[:5]
```

One caveat Vaathiyaar insists you memorize: the reranker has a **recall ceiling**. It can only promote documents stage 1 handed it. If the right answer wasn't in the top-50 candidates, no reranker on earth can bring it back â€” widen stage 1, don't blame stage 2.

### Why This Model, Specifically?

At ~23M parameters it scores a pair in a few milliseconds on CPU, ships in PyTorch, ONNX, and safetensors, and lifts retrieval quality enough that LlamaIndex, Haystack, and most production RAG stacks treat reranking as a default step â€” including as an optional rerank stage for a local RAG pipeline like Homie's.

> **Key Insight:** A bi-encoder answers "what is this text about?" once, forever. A cross-encoder answers "does THIS text answer THIS question?" fresh, per pair. The first is cheap and approximate, the second is expensive and sharp â€” and two-stage retrieval is simply the discipline of spending the expensive model only on the shortlist the cheap one nominates.

instruction.en: Build a toy cross-encoder. A real one scores a (query, document) pair by reading both together; your toy version captures the same contract with term coverage. Write `score_pair(query, doc)` that lowercases both texts, splits them on whitespace, and returns the fraction of query tokens that appear anywhere in the document, rounded to 4 decimals. Print `score_pair("fix python import error", "how to fix an import error in python")` and then `score_pair("fix python import error", "python list comprehension guide")` â€” the relevant doc must score higher.

practice_challenges.test_code:
assert score_pair("fix python import error", "how to fix an import error in python") == 1.0, f"all 4 query terms are present, expected 1.0: {score_pair('fix python import error', 'how to fix an import error in python')}"
assert score_pair("fix python import error", "python list comprehension guide") == 0.25, f"only 'python' matches, expected 0.25: {score_pair('fix python import error', 'python list comprehension guide')}"
assert score_pair("a b", "x y") == 0.0, "no overlap must score 0.0"
assert score_pair("Python", "python rocks") == 1.0, "matching must be case-insensitive"
assert score_pair("speed up pandas merges", "pandas speed tips") == 0.5, "2 of 4 query tokens match -> 0.5"
print("All tests passed!")

instruction.en: Now wire up the full two-stage pipeline. Write `two_stage_search(docs, bi_scores, cross_scores, k1, k2)`: stage 1 keeps the k1 documents with the highest bi-encoder scores (the recall net); stage 2 reranks ONLY those survivors by their cross-encoder scores and returns the top-k2 document names, best first. Print `two_stage_search(["a", "b", "c", "d"], [0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.2], [0.1, 0.4, 0.95, 0.99], 3, 2)` â€” note that "d" has the best cross score of all but must NOT appear: stage 1 never handed it to the reranker. That is the recall ceiling.

practice_challenges.starter_code:
def two_stage_search(docs: list, bi_scores: list, cross_scores: list, k1: int, k2: int) -> list:
    """Stage 1: top-k1 by bi_score. Stage 2: rerank survivors by cross_score, return top-k2."""
    # 1. stage1 = indices 0..len(docs)-1 sorted by bi_scores[i], highest first, sliced to k1
    # 2. reranked = those surviving indices sorted by cross_scores[i], highest first
    # 3. return the doc names for the first k2 reranked indices
    pass

print(two_stage_search(["a", "b", "c", "d"], [0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.2], [0.1, 0.4, 0.95, 0.99], 3, 2))

en: stage1 = sorted(range(len(docs)), key=lambda i: bi_scores[i], reverse=True)[:k1]
Rerank the SAME index list by the other score: sorted(stage1, key=lambda i: cross_scores[i], reverse=True)
Finish with [docs[i] for i in reranked[:k2]]

practice_challenges.test_code:
r = two_stage_search(["a", "b", "c", "d"], [0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.2], [0.1, 0.4, 0.95, 0.99], 3, 2)
assert r == ["c", "b"], f"expected ['c', 'b'], got {r}"
assert "d" not in r, "recall ceiling: 'd' was cut in stage 1, the reranker cannot resurrect it"
assert two_stage_search(["a", "b"], [0.1, 0.9], [0.9, 0.1], 2, 1) == ["a"], "when k1 keeps everyone, only the cross score decides"
assert two_stage_search(["a", "b", "c"], [0.9, 0.8, 0.1], [0.0, 1.0, 5.0], 2, 1) == ["b"], "'c' scores 5.0 but never survived stage 1"
assert two_stage_search(["x"], [1.0], [1.0], 1, 1) == ["x"], "single-doc corpus passes straight through"
print("All tests passed!")

q.en: Why can't ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 precompute scores for all documents ahead of time?
q.ta: ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2 ஏன் எல்லா ஆவணங்களுக்கும் மதிப்பெண்களை முன்கூட்டியே கணக்கிட முடியாது?

en: It only runs on GPUs, not during indexing
Its 384-dim vectors take too long to save
Each score depends on the query, read together with the doc
The model is too large to store the results

q.en: Stage 1 uses top_k=50, but the right answer ranks 80th in vector search. What actually fixes this?
q.ta: Stage 1-இல் top_k=50 பயன்படுத்தப்படுகிறது, ஆனால் சரியான பதில் vector search-இல் 80-ஆவது இடத்தில் உள்ளது. இதை உண்மையில் சரிசெய்வது எது?

en: Run the reranker twice on the same 50
Widen stage 1, e.g. raise top_k above 80
Use a stronger cross-encoder in stage 2
ta: அதே 50 ஆவணங்களில் reranker-ஐ இரண்டு முறை இயக்குவது
stage 1-ஐ விரிவாக்குவது, எ.கா. top_k-ஐ 80-க்கு மேல் உயர்த்துவது
அதற்குப் பதிலாக reverse=False கொண்டு rerank செய்வது

q.en: A student's score_pair ends with return round(hits / len(doc_tokens), 4). What's the mistake?
q.ta: ஒரு மாணவரின் score_pair, return round(hits / len(doc_tokens), 4) என்று முடிகிறது. இதில் உள்ள தவறு என்ன?

en: It should divide by the number of query tokens
It should round to 2 decimals, not 4
The texts must not be lowercased first
doc_tokens should be a list, not a set

doc_tokens ஒரு set ஆக இல்லாமல் list ஆக இருக்க வேண்டும்

uth_example:
query = "speed up pandas joins"
docs = ["speed up your car", "make pandas joins faster", "pandas merge is slow"]
SYN = {"faster": "speed", "merge": "joins"}        # meaning only visible when read together

def bi_score(q, d):                  # bi-encoder: texts compared separately, word overlap
    return len(set(q.split()) & set(d.split()))

def cross_score(q, d):               # cross-encoder: reads query AND doc as one input
    dw = {SYN.get(w, w) for w in d.split()}
    qw = q.split()
    matched = sum(1 for w in qw if w in dw)
    return matched + (2 if "pandas" in qw and "pandas" in dw else 0)

stage1 = sorted(docs, key=lambda d: bi_score(query, d), reverse=True)     # fast recall
scores = {d: cross_score(query, d) for d in stage1}                       # slow, precise
stage2 = sorted(stage1, key=scores.get, reverse=True)
print("bi-encoder order:   ", stage1)
print("cross-encoder order:", stage2, scores)
